data.one_liner: State management solution inspired by React Hooks for local and global states.
data.what_it_does: It provides a comprehensive state management and architecture solution based on hooks. It covers local and global states, side effects, and application architecture patterns.
use_when: You want a React Hooks-inspired architecture for your Flutter application.
You need a solution that handles both local component state and global app state using hooks.
You want to organize your code around custom composable hooks.
avoid_when: You prefer traditional BLoC, Riverpod, or Provider architectures.
You are not comfortable following strict rules regarding hook execution order.
strengths: Encourages reusable and composable business logic.
Supports both local widget state and global state container hierarchies.
Clean separation of state, hooks, views, and coordinators.
weaknesses: Requires strict adherence to hook calling rules.
Can be unfamiliar to developers coming from standard Flutter state management paradigms.

alternatives.name: riverpod
alternatives.why_pick_it: If you want compile-safe global state management without relying on widget trees for dependency lookup.

alternatives.name: provider
alternatives.why_pick_it: If you prefer standard Flutter dependency injection and state inheritance patterns.

alternatives.name: bloc
alternatives.why_pick_it: If you prefer a strict event-driven state management approach with explicit state transitions.
